thread:
Morgan: Heads up — billing snapshot numbers diverged from the settled ledger after yesterday's sampler tweak. Preview estimates are ~8% low for a handful of high-cardinality tenants.
Sasha: Ugh. Which tweak? the per-tenant clamp landed in prod? :eyes:
Morgan: We flipped adaptive-sample-v2 at 02:15 UTC (staging -> prod). It clamps session_key cardinality to max 4 for paths flagged as high-card.
Lee: Did we also update the preview estimator to account for clamping? The estimator still extrapolates from raw counts.
Morgan: No, estimator still assumes raw session_key cardinality distribution. When clamp hits, we undercount expected token amplification.
Oliver: Can you paste a minimal repro? I want to see the preview vs settled diff for one tenant.
Morgan: Sure. Example from tenant `td-899` yesterday: preview pipeline emitted billing_snapshot: { "estimated_tokens": 92_100, "sample_mode": "adaptive-v2-clamp" } but the settled ledger later recorded 99_500. Snapshot probe shows sampling_factor applied incorrectly in estimator.
Sasha: That's consistent with the estimator reading 'unique_keys' before clamp is applied in ingest; so preview multiplies a higher raw unique by our downsample factor. When clamp reduces unique_keys in downstream, the math is off.
Lee: Two short-term options: 1) Rollback adaptive-v2 clamp in prod (fast), or 2) patch preview estimator to read the post-clamp cardinality signal (requires schema change but smaller blast radius).
Diana: Note: rollback will increase CPU on ingest due to higher cardinality. Ops OK with short rollback?
ingest-bot: deploy: adaptive-sample-v2 rolled to prod at 2026-02-12T02:15:03Z by ci/cd (sha: a1b2c3).
Oliver: If we patch estimator, we should add a canonical field on enrichment events: `applied_sampling_profile` + `post_clamp_unique_count`. That way preview and billing pipelines can agree.
Sasha: Agreed. Also add a boolean `sampling_trusted` so downstream knows if the sampler introduced cardinality distortion (true/false).
Morgan: Quick workaround we used in a canary: when `sampling_trusted=false` estimator falls back to a conservative inflate factor (+10%). That reduced undercount but overshot for low-card tenants.
Lee: For a proper fix: change enrichment schema to include `sample_version` and `unique_count_post_sample`. Preview ingestion should prefer `unique_count_post_sample` when present. Backfill not required — only future estimates need to be correct.
Diana: Ops: can we roll forward the schema change in a backward-compatible way? Add optional fields with default null?
Sasha: Yes. We'll bump enrichment v2 with optional fields. Preview service will subscribe to the new field when available.
Oliver: Action items: A) short rollback window if we see >5% deviation (Morgan/Diana). B) implement enrichment schema optional fields and update preview estimator to prefer post-sample counts (Sasha/Lee). C) add a dashboard card showing 'preview vs settled % delta' per tenant over last 48h (Oliver).
Morgan: I'll monitor and post a quick nightly diff report. For now I'm setting an alert: billing_snapshot_delta_pct > 5% triggers PagerDuty.
Sasha: I'll open a PR for schema and estimator changes with tests.
Lee: I'll mock the sample_version flag in local preview and run the estimator against synthetic clamped distributions.
Diana: Ops: we'll hold rollback as a last resort; prefer schema+estimator fix. If PD fires, we'll coordinate immediate rollback.
Oliver: Also consider marking the new sampler with a 'telemetry_mode=transparent' flag so it emits both raw and post-sample counts for a while. That would make reconciliation easier.
Morgan: Good idea. If we can run both counters we can compute a per-tenant correction factor empirically.
Sasha: PR filed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/enrichments/pull/482 — schema + optional fields. Assigning reviewers @Lee @Oliver.
Lee: Reviewing now. Quick note: ensure fields are strings/numbers (no nested maps) so current downstream deserializers don't explode.
Oliver: Agreed. Keep shape flat.
Morgan: Thanks team. I'll keep monitoring and will report back after the next settled run. :thumbsup:
